routes.history: The Qhapaq Ñan was the Inca road system, a network of roughly 40,000 km across what are now Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. Relay stations for chasqui runners stood at short intervals, and tambos a day's walk apart supplied travellers and llama herds. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.
routes.story: Messages travelled by relay: one chasqui ran a short stage and passed the message and knotted-cord quipu to the next runner. Llama trains carried loads along the same road, and the llama was the only beast of burden in the Inca Empire.
